scope: Explicit owner-requested narration pacing refinement; not routine production review

method.route: Registry transcriber, local faster-whisper base/en, word_timestamps=True, vad_filter=True, CPU int8; HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 for reference runs
method.wall_clock_wpm: Recognized lexical word tokens assigned by timestamp midpoint per full elapsed window, multiplied by60/window seconds. Includes narrative pauses.
method.word_span_coverage_pct: Union of inferred word intervals divided by elapsed window; an ASR timing proxy, not acoustic voiced-time measurement.
method.pause_proxy: Gaps between adjacent recognized words >=0.3s; portions clipped at window bounds, count assigned by gap midpoint. Not acoustic silence, and music/effects may continue.
method.bin_comparison: Nonoverlapping complete30s bins; incomplete final bin excluded from variability statistics, retained in full-film and ending metrics.
method.narrative_windows: Editorial windows selected from prior visual/transcript study and saved chapter cues, not frame-exact narration boundaries or normalized story phases.
method.confidence: Model base may miss or hallucinate words; word boundaries are approximate. No audible alignment verification.

limitations: No audible playback; results do not establish voice identity, accent, timbre, emotion, performance quality, music audibility or speech/music level ratio.
No inference that larger pause share is inherently better or that every gap is an intentional dramatic pause.
Different titles and durations are not controlled experiments; story-role differences matter.
Reference factual assertions are not validated by ASR.
Full copyrighted transcripts are retained only in temporary local research caches; this public report contains timing aggregates only.

asr_hook_landmarks.caveat: ASR estimates; revise earlier visual-only hook-duration guesses, not a universal hook target.

music_feedback: Owner explicitly says sample score is too loud. That perceptual correction is authoritative; these timing measurements do not provide a reference-matched dB target.
